The table summarizes the UV index value recorded by a research assistant at noon each day for 49 days.
UV indexNumber of days
19
215
312
413
According to the table, a UV index value of 1 was recorded on how many days?
whyCorrect: Read the row whose UV index is 1 and take the value in the second column. That column counts days, so 9 days had a UV index of 1. No arithmetic is needed; the trap is reading the wrong column or adding rows together.

whyWrong.A: 4 is the largest UV index in the first column, not a count of days.
whyWrong.C: 40 is the total number of days for indexes 2, 3 and 4 combined — the days that were not index 1.
whyWrong.D: 49 is the total number of days observed, the sum of the whole second column.

stem:
The table shows the number of trees planted for 4 separate plots of land on a tree farm.
PlotTrees planted
Plot 185
Plot 295
Plot 3100
Plot 478
What is the maximum number of trees planted on one of these 4 plots of land?
whyCorrect: "Maximum" means the largest single value in the data, not the largest possible reading on the scale and not an average. Compare the four counts and take the biggest: 100, at Plot 3.

whyWrong.D: 78 is Plot 4, the minimum rather than the maximum.

note: Source prints this as a bar graph (Plot 1-4 against trees planted, axis to 110). Bar heights are exactly the four answer choices, so it is rendered here as an equivalent table.

stem: The dot plot shown gives the distribution of values in a data set. What is the minimum value in the data set?
whyCorrect: The minimum is the smallest value that actually occurs, so read the position of the leftmost column of dots on the number line, not how many dots are stacked there. The leftmost stack sits at 11, so the minimum value is 11.

whyWrong.A: 1 is not a value on the number line at all; it looks like the count of the shortest stack.
whyWrong.B: 2 is the height of the leftmost stack — how many times 11 occurs, not the value itself.
whyWrong.C: 9 is a tick on the axis with no dots above it, so no data point takes that value.

note: Dot plot on a number line labelled 10-17. Dot counts: 11 -> 2, 12 -> 3, 13 -> 5, 14 -> 5, 15 -> 4, 16 -> 1 (no dots at 10 or 17), 20 values in total. Not converted to a table because questions 13 and 15 in the same section are the same question presented as a frequency table.

stem:
The table shows the frequency of values in a data set.
ValueFrequency
119
181
259
3215
What is the minimum value of the data set?
whyCorrect: The data set is the values in the left column, each repeated as many times as the right column says. The frequency column never contributes a data value, so the minimum is the smallest entry in the Value column: 11.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smallest number in the Frequency column — it is how often 18 occurs, not a value in the data set.
whyWrong.B: 9 is a frequency, not a value.
whyWrong.D: 18 is a value in the data set but not the smallest one; 11 is smaller.

138

What is the minimum value of the data set?
whyCorrect: Only the Value column holds data; the Frequency column just says how many times each value appears. The smallest value listed is 13, and it does occur (frequency 8), so the minimum is 13.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smallest frequency, not the smallest value.
whyWrong.B: 8 is a frequency, not a value in the data set.
whyWrong.D: 20 is in the data set but 13 is smaller.

What is the minimum value of the data set?
whyCorrect: The data set consists of the numbers in the Value column; the Frequency column only counts repeats. The smallest value listed is 120, and its frequency of 3 confirms it actually occurs, so the minimum is 120.

whyWrong.A: 1 is the smallest frequency (how often 160 occurs), not a data value.
whyWrong.B: 3 is the frequency of 120, not the value itself.
whyWrong.D: 160 is the maximum value, not the minimum.

stem:
1, 4, 7, 10, 33

What is the mean of the data shown?
whyCorrect: Add all five values and divide by 5: 1 + 4 + 7 + 10 + 33 = 55, and 55 ÷ 5 = 11. The single large value, 33, pulls the mean above the middle value, which is why the mean here is not the same as the median.

whyWrong.A: 7 is the median — the middle value once the list is ordered — not the mean.
whyWrong.C: 17 is the mean of just the smallest and largest values, (1 + 33) ÷ 2; it ignores the other three numbers.
whyWrong.D: 33 is the largest value, i.e. the maximum, not an average.
